From bd0687c18e635b63233dc87f38058cd728802ab4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Magnus Karlsson <magnus.karlsson@intel.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2021 11:26:07 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] xsk: Do not sleep in poll() when need_wakeup set

Do not sleep in poll() when the need_wakeup flag is set. When this
flag is set, the application needs to explicitly wake up the driver
with a syscall (poll, recvmsg, sendmsg, etc.) to guarantee that Rx
and/or Tx processing will be processed promptly. But the current code
in poll(), sleeps first then wakes up the driver. This means that no
driver processing will occur (baring any interrupts) until the timeout
has expired.

Fix this by checking the need_wakeup flag first and if set, wake the
driver and return to the application. Only if need_wakeup is not set
should the process sleep if there is a timeout set in the poll() call.

Fixes: 77cd0d7b3f25 ("xsk: add support for need_wakeup flag in AF_XDP rings")
Reported-by: Keith Wiles <keith.wiles@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Magnus Karlsson <magnus.karlsson@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Acked-by: Maciej Fijalkowski <maciej.fijalkowski@intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20211214102607.7677-1-magnus.karlsson@gmail.com

diff --git a/net/xdp/xsk.c b/net/xdp/xsk.c
index f16074eb53c7..7a466ea962c5 100644
--- a/net/xdp/xsk.c
+++ b/net/xdp/xsk.c
@@ -677,8 +677,6 @@ static __poll_t xsk_poll(struct file *file, struct socket *sock,
 	struct xdp_sock *xs = xdp_sk(sk);
 	struct xsk_buff_pool *pool;
 
-	sock_poll_wait(file, sock, wait);
-
 	if (unlikely(!xsk_is_bound(xs)))
 		return mask;
 
@@ -690,6 +688,8 @@ static __poll_t xsk_poll(struct file *file, struct socket *sock,
 		else
 			/* Poll needs to drive Tx also in copy mode */
 			__xsk_sendmsg(sk);
+	} else {
+		sock_poll_wait(file, sock, wait);
 	}
 
 	if (xs->rx && !xskq_prod_is_empty(xs->rx))
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/xdp/xsk.c`**
1. Removed the line `sock_poll_wait(file, sock, wait);` from the beginning of the `xsk_poll` function.
2. Added a conditional check for the `need_wakeup` flag:
   - If `need_wakeup` is set, the function now directly wakes the driver and returns to the application without sleeping.
   - If `need_wakeup` is not set, the function calls `sock_poll_wait(file, sock, wait);` to allow the process to sleep if there is a timeout set in the `poll()` call.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `xsk.c` are aimed at improving the behavior of the `poll()` function in relation to the `need_wakeup` flag. The change ensures that when the `need_wakeup` flag is set, the application can immediately wake the driver without unnecessary delays caused by sleeping. This directly addresses the issue where the driver processing would not occur until a timeout expired, thus enhancing the responsiveness of the system when the application requires immediate attention from the driver. The relationship between the removal of the initial sleep and the conditional check for `need_wakeup` is crucial, as it allows for more efficient handling of driver interactions based on the application's needs.

```

```

If the flag is set, it directly wakes up the driver using `xsk_wakeup()` or processes Tx operations without sleeping. This ensures that the driver can respond promptly to the application's needs, thus fixing the bug.
